messages.text: Does the Presidents Cup need changing to stop Team USA’s dominance?

metadata.summary: The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? A different format? Fewer points on offer? LIV Golf players involved? Extra team events on the schedule? We look at possible ways to make the Presidents Cup even more competitive, following the United States' record-extending 11th consecutive win over the International Team Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 28 September 2026 12:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the Presidents Cup, where Team USA dominated the Sunday singles to close out a comeback victory over the International Team The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest. Brandt Snedeker's side produced the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history at Medinah, winning 9.5 of the 12 points on offer in the Sunday singles to close out a record-extending 11th consecutive victory. A 17-13 winning margin doesn't tell the full picture from a closer-than-expected contest, including a foursomes session sweep for the Internationals on Friday and them leading going into the final day for just the fourth time ever. messages.text: Matos on Swansea's fast start and working with Klopp at Liverpool

metadata.summary: It is Swansea City who sit top of the Championship after eight games. Not something many would have expected at the start of the season.
metadata.content: Vitor Matos interview: Swansea City boss on their fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Vitor Matos interview: Swansea City boss on their fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool Vitor Matos speaks to Sky Sports about Swansea City's fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. Watch Swansea City vs Norwich City live on Sky Sports+ and the Sky Sports app at 12.30pm on Saturday October 10 Simeon Gholam EFL Editor @simeongholam Monday 28 September 2026 11:33, UK It is Swansea City who sit top of the Championship after eight games. Not something many would have expected at the start of the season. But Vitor Matos and his high-pressing, energetic side have enjoyed a wonderful opening to the campaign. It is performances, more than results, that have pleased him. "I'm happy with the start more than the results," Matos - who won Sky Bet Championship Manager of the Month for August - tells Sky Sports . "It's the style and the feeling that when you go to watch us play, you have a good feeling. We are happy when you are out, especially our fans. That's what we wanted, that's what we are trying more than anything. "So far, it's been good." messages.text: Norris apologises for Colapinto comments following Azerbaijan GP crash

metadata.summary: Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash Franco Colapinto caused a collision with his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris that took all three of them out of the Azerbaijan GP; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Monday 28 September 2026 11:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Colapinto triggered the accident during a Safety Car restart in Baku when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside. Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident in Saturday's race, Norris said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1" and called for such incidents to result in one-race bans for the initiator. messages.text: Why Man City charges case could still drag on for years

metadata.summary: Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded.

City insist they have irrefutable evidence to prove they did not break the rules Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded. According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage. In 2014, City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play (FFP) rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m (£25.7m) for breaking the rules again. messages.text: Broncos score in final minute to beat Rams in thrilling comeback

metadata.summary: Bo Nix crossed for a touchdown from close range with 47 seconds left in the fourth quarter as the Denver Broncos came from 16-0 down at half-time to beat the Los Angeles Rams 30-26.
metadata.content: Los Angeles Rams 26-30 Denver Broncos: Bo Nix scores in final minute of fourth quarter to complete thrilling comeback | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Los Angeles Rams 26-30 Denver Broncos: Bo Nix scores in final minute of fourth quarter to complete thrilling comeback Bo Nix scored in the final minute as the Broncos came from behind to beat the Los Angeles Rams 30-26 in Denver; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI Monday 28 September 2026 06:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Los Angeles Rams at the Denver Broncos from Week 3 of the NFL season Bo Nix crossed for a touchdown from close range with 47 seconds left in the fourth quarter as the Denver Broncos came from 16-0 down at half-time to beat the Los Angeles Rams 30-26. Quarterback Nix's keeper from inches outside the goal line capped a wild final five minutes that included a 66-yard pick-6 by Denver and a quick touchdown response by Los Angeles. After Nix put the Broncos (2-1) in front by reaching over the scrum with both hands gripping the football, Matthew Stafford, whose 17 comebacks in the last 2 minutes are the most by any active quarterback, drove the Rams to the Denver 14, where he spiked the ball with 2 seconds left. messages.text: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'

metadata.summary: Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.
metadata.content: Kevin Pietersen promises to challenge Brendon McCullum as England white-ball head coach eyes world No 1 ranking | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Kevin Pietersen promises to challenge Brendon McCullum as England white-ball head coach eyes world No 1 ranking England's new white-ball specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen tells Sky Sports Cricket: "There are times when Harry Brook stands at the wicket and he goes, 'This is too easy'" but adds: "I will never in my life try and take the flair and that genius out of him" Monday 28 September 2026 07:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Pietersen speaks to Nasser Hussain about his new role as an England white-ball mentor and how his relationship with Brendon McCullum has developed Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in. Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over. Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday.
